subject: Embedding vendor migration: risk checklist & ops playbook
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmedata.com>, Jill Huang <jill.huang@acmedata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Embedding vendor migration: risk checklist & ops playbook

Hi Samir / Jill —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of what we heard:
- You currently host embeddings with VectorCo (proprietary) and see ~150M vectors (1536 dim) for product search + personalization.
- Concern areas: auth/keys rotation, batching throughput at query time, normalization differences (VectorCo stores L2-normalized vectors), and reranker integration latency.
- Target: migrate to Redwood embeddings for lower unit cost, unified auth, and tighter routing to reranker without user-visible latency regressions.

2) Immediate technical asks we promised to follow up on:
- Exact vector dims and any mixed-width variants (you mentioned historical 1536 + a small 768 set).
- Typical query QPS and burst profile (search request vs offline scoring).
- Current batching pipeline and any per-request normalization.
- SSO/KMS constraints for key storage and rotation cadence.

3) Proposed next steps (timeline suggestion):
- This week: exchange the CSV export of sample vectors + query logs (anonymized) — Acme -> Redwood.
- By EOD Wed: Redwood will run a small compatibility test (dim/float->quantization fit) and return a short report.
- Next Tue: 30-min tech sync between Ben (runtime), Logan (ops), and your infra lead to confirm routing and canary strategy.

Attachments: I am including the first draft of an "Embed Migration Playbook" (attachment) that highlights the migration phases, canary gating, and rollback criteria.

If that all looks right, I will schedule the tech sync and open a HubSpot opportunity with the proposed delivery milestones.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(k) +1-415-555-0192

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmedata.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding vendor migration: risk checklist & ops playbook

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Vector dimensions: main index is 1536 (user-facing vectors). We also have a smaller legacy index at 768 used for a narrow personalization feature — not latency-sensitive.
- Current QPS: baseline 120 QPS with 800 QPS bursts (peak during promos). Average query size ~3 candidates per session but search fanout can be 50 for exploration.
- Batching: we batch on a 20ms window in front of VectorCo; backend has a weighted sampler that sometimes forces single-vector queries for freshness.
- Normalization: VectorCo stores L2-normalized vectors; downstream reranker expects dot-product scores (we denormalize in ML infra before reranking today).
- Security: keys are stored in AWS KMS; rotation every 60 days. We have a pending compliance check for bringing any KMS-backed keys into third-party infra.

I attached a sanitized sample export (acme-embeddings-current-config.csv) with vector dims and timestamps for ~10k vectors. Please confirm Redwood can run a normalization/batching compatibility pass without us exposing user ids.

Also: procurement asked for an estimate of contract length and an outline of the SLA gating for canary phases. Can Marissa share a short one-pager?

Thanks,
Samir
Senior ML Eng, Acme Data

---
Attachment stubs: acme-embeddings-current-config.csv (10k rows)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmedata.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embedding vendor migration: risk checklist & ops playbook

Samir — great details, thanks. Technical notes and proposed quick POC we can run on your sample export: 

1) Dim mapping: we can import both 1536 and 768 indexes. For the 1536 set we will evaluate quantization to int8/4-bit for storage; we'll report expected recall delta. 768 set we recommend keeping in float32 until we confirm no quality regression.

2) Normalization handling: Redwood supports both L2-normalized and raw vectors. For your reranker pipeline we suggest keeping the same denormalization step server-side (Redwood can optionally emit normalization metadata in the response so your reranker can compute dot-product without extra infra changes). We'll include a sample response format showing norm / raw scores.

3) Batching & throughput: Redwood runtime supports sub-20ms batching windows; we will replicate your 20ms behavior in the POC. For bursts we recommend a hybrid routing policy — primary pool optimized for latency (lower batch sizes) and overflow pool for throughput (larger batch sizes). We can simulate 800 QPS bursts using your logs.

4) KMS / auth: For Private mode we can integrate with your AWS KMS and rotate keys per your cadence. For Hosted accounts we propose KMS-wrapped keys with a customer-managed key option if procurement requires it.

POC plan (timeline):
- Wed (48h): Redwood runs compatibility pass against the CSV and returns a short quant/recall estimate + suggested quant profile.
- Next Tue: tech sync to agree on canary gating metrics (latency P95, recall delta <= 1.5% for top-10, error budget).

I'll attach a short sample JSON response layout and a stubbed canary gating checklist. If the team approves, we'll spin up a sandbox index and share credentials (ephemeral) for your infra to test the reranker integration.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
